text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A organizes its argument into distinct body paragraphs each addressing a separate supporting point (fuel savings, safety measures, affordability of technology), with a clear introduction and conclusion restating the thesis.", "quality": "Structured organization", "description": "The essay presents a clear thesis and develops each supporting point in its own paragraph with an introduction and conclusion that frame the argument."}, {"evidence": "Essay A quotes the article directly, e.g., 'the cars he forsees would use half the fuel of today's taxis' (paragraph 1), and cites paragraph numbers for evidence.", "quality": "Use of textual evidence", "description": "The essay grounds its claims in specific quoted details from the source article with citations, rather than making unsupported assertions."}, {"evidence": "Essay A explains how each point supports the position, e.g., connecting reduced fuel use to affordability and accessibility for less financially well-off drivers.", "quality": "Reasoned elaboration", "description": "The essay develops each piece of evidence by explaining its implications and how it advances the argument for driverless cars."}, {"evidence": "Essay A maintains a consistent argumentative stance throughout, with each body paragraph explicitly linking back to why development should continue.", "quality": "Coherent argumentative focus", "description": "The essay sustains a clear position and ties every section back to that central claim, keeping the argument unified."}, {"evidence": "Essay B offers only brief, general statements such as 'Self-driving cars will be great and will keep the road saffer' without developing reasons or using article details.", "quality": "Depth of development", "description": "Essay A develops its claims with multiple supporting details and explanation, whereas Essay B states opinions without substantive elaboration."}]}
